chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from some of our companions, and from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) disliked slaughtering and shedding blood on Friday before the prayer, except out of necessity.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering animals on Friday before the prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the spiritual gravity of the Friday congregational prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) by linking physical acts of slaughter to potential ritual or environmental distraction. The ruling of *karahat* (recommended dislike) rather than strict prohibition reflects the juristic balance between maintaining the sanctity of the prayer time and accommodating practical necessities, such as preparing food for guests or immediate consumption.
